title: Englisch 8 Realschule (ZAM Academy)
description: 51 Lektionen mit englischen Materialien zu Geschichte Nordamerikas, USA, New York, Kanada, Sprachwerkstatt und amerikanischer Jugendliteratur, Sprachaufgaben auf zwei Stufen und 102 gezielten Wiederholungsfragen. LehrplanPLUS Bayern, gemeinsamer Lernpfad; natürliche Hörtexte, Gespräche und eine ganze Lektüre ergänzen die App.

atoms.title: Many nations, many ways of life

practice_items.question: You need the number of tribes that are recognised today. Which reading technique fits best?
practice_items.concept: Scanning: I look quickly for the number.

options: Scanning: I look quickly for the number.
Reading every word slowly from the start.

practice_items.question: Why is the name of a nation, e.g. “the Lakota”, more precise than “the Indians”?
practice_items.concept: There were and are many different nations with their own languages and ways of life.
practice_items.sample_solution: “The Indians” puts very different peoples into one group. Naming the nation, for example the Lakota or the Cherokee, shows that each nation has its own language, history and rules.

atoms.title: Two settlements, two points of view

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Many nations, many ways of life“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: You rewrite a settler's diary from a Wampanoag point of view. What must stay the same?
practice_items.concept: The historical facts, such as the date and the place.

options: The historical facts, such as the date and the place.
The settler's feelings and opinions.

practice_items.question: What was Jamestown in Virginia, founded in 1607?
practice_items.concept: The first permanent English colony in North America.
practice_items.sample_solution: Jamestown was founded in 1607 and was the first English colony in North America that lasted. The Pilgrims came later, in 1620, and built Plymouth.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Two settlements, two points of view“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: What did the 13th Amendment to the U.S. Constitution do in 1865?
practice_items.concept: It abolished slavery in the United States.

options: It abolished slavery in the United States.
It started the American Civil War.

practice_items.question: What happened in the colony of Virginia in 1619?
practice_items.concept: The arrival of Africans was recorded there for the first time.
practice_items.sample_solution: In 1619 about twenty Africans who had been taken by force arrived in Virginia. It is the first recorded arrival of Africans in the English colony; slavery developed from such beginnings.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „From 1619 to the 13th Amendment“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Why was Rosa Parks arrested in Montgomery in 1955?
practice_items.concept: She refused to give up her bus seat for white passengers.

options: She refused to give up her bus seat for white passengers.
She refused to pay for her bus ticket.

practice_items.question: What did the Civil Rights Act of 1964 make illegal?
practice_items.concept: Discrimination in public places and at work.
practice_items.sample_solution: President Johnson signed the Civil Rights Act in 1964. It prohibited discrimination in public places, made discrimination at work illegal and supported the integration of schools.

atoms.title: Explaining the Underground Railroad in German

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „From 1619 to the 13th Amendment“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Your grandmother asks what the “Underground Railroad” was. Which German explanation is best?
practice_items.concept: Ein geheimes Netz von Fluchtwegen und Helfern für Versklavte.

options: Ein geheimes Netz von Fluchtwegen und Helfern für Versklavte.
Eine unterirdische Eisenbahn für Flüchtlinge.

practice_items.question: What does the term “freedom seeker” mean in texts about the Underground Railroad?
practice_items.concept: An enslaved person who escaped to become free.
practice_items.sample_solution: The National Park Service uses “freedom seeker” instead of words like “runaway”: it describes enslaved African Americans who escaped from slavery to gain their freedom.

atoms.title: Fifty states and a capital district

practice_items.question: Is Washington, D.C. one of the 50 U.S. states?
practice_items.concept: No, it is a federal district, the District of Columbia.

options: No, it is a federal district, the District of Columbia.
Yes, it is the smallest of the 50 states.

practice_items.question: What does every U.S. state have of its own, according to the fact sheet?
practice_items.concept: Its own capital, government and laws.
practice_items.sample_solution: Each of the 50 states has its own capital, its own government and its own laws, for example on the age for a driver's license. Washington, D.C. is a federal district, not a state.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Fifty states and a capital district“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: The chart shows 30 storm reports in April and 60 in May. Which sentence describes this correctly?
practice_items.concept: May had twice as many reports as April.

options: May had twice as many reports as April.
April had twice as many reports as May.

practice_items.question: From when to when does the Atlantic hurricane season officially run?
practice_items.concept: From June 1 to November 30.
practice_items.sample_solution: According to the U.S. National Hurricane Center, the Atlantic hurricane season runs from June 1 to November 30, so the coasts prepare in summer and autumn.

practice_items.question: Which conclusion can you really draw from the two interviews?
practice_items.concept: Both want to go to college, but their free time is very different.

options: Both want to go to college, but their free time is very different.
All American teenagers live in suburbs with big gardens.

practice_items.question: What does “social range” mean when people talk about life in the USA?
practice_items.concept: The big differences in how well-off people are and how they live.
practice_items.sample_solution: Social range describes the differences between rich and poor families, for example in housing, free time and chances for college. One interview cannot show the whole range.

atoms.title: Island of hope, island of tears

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Two settlements, two points of view“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Why was Ellis Island also called an “Island of Tears”?
practice_items.concept: Some families were separated and some people were sent back.

options: Some families were separated and some people were sent back.
The weather on the island was always rainy.

practice_items.question: What was Ellis Island from 1892 to 1924?
practice_items.concept: America's largest immigration station, in New York Harbor.
practice_items.sample_solution: From 1892 to 1924 more than 12 million immigrants were processed on Ellis Island. For most it was an “Island of Hope”; for some it became an “Island of Tears”.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Storms in a bar chart“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which phrase starts a letter to the editor that refers to the website?
practice_items.concept: I read your page on saving water with great interest.

options: I read your page on saving water with great interest.
Hi guys, what's up?

practice_items.question: What do you do first in a letter to the editor?
practice_items.concept: Refer to the text you are answering.
practice_items.sample_solution: A letter to the editor starts with a reference such as “I read your article on …”. Then you give your opinion with reasons and end with a suggestion or a clear conclusion.

atoms.title: A radio ad and a store announcement

practice_items.question: Which trick does the radio ad use when it says “but only until Sunday”?
practice_items.concept: It puts time pressure on the listeners.

options: It puts time pressure on the listeners.
It gives a neutral fact about the shoes.

practice_items.question: An announcement says one thing and then “sorry – that's …”. Which information counts?
practice_items.concept: The corrected information after “sorry – that's …”.
practice_items.sample_solution: Speakers often correct themselves in announcements. The second version after “sorry” or “I mean” replaces the first one, so you note the correction.

atoms.title: Silicon Valley and a set-up guide

practice_items.question: In the guide, the light turns red. What should you do?
practice_items.concept: Unplug it, wait ten seconds and start again.

options: Unplug it, wait ten seconds and start again.
Hold the button for five seconds once more.

practice_items.question: Which verb form do instructions in English usually use, e.g. “Plug in the cable.”?
practice_items.concept: The imperative: the base form without a subject.
practice_items.sample_solution: Instructions use the imperative, for example “Plug in the cable” or “Do not open the case”, together with sequence words such as first, next, then and finally.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Fifty states and a capital district“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: A U.S. form asks for your date of birth as MM/DD/YYYY. You were born on 7 March 2012. What do you write?
What do “surname” and “given name” mean on an English form?
practice_items.concept: Surname is the family name; given name is the first name.
practice_items.sample_solution: On forms, “surname” or “last name” asks for your family name (e.g. Weber) and “given name” or “first name” for your first name(s) (e.g. Lena Maria).

practice_items.question: On the phone you are not sure about a price. What do you say?
practice_items.concept: Sorry, did you say 114 or 140?

options: Sorry, did you say 114 or 140?
Price is wrong, give me another.

practice_items.question: How do you politely say that you want to book a room?
practice_items.concept: I'd like to book a room, please.
practice_items.sample_solution: “I'd like to book a double room for two nights, please.” I'd like to (= I would like to) is a polite way to say what you want in a service situation.

atoms.title: At the doctor's: helping your dad

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Explaining the Underground Railroad in German“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: You don't know the English word for “Knöchel”. What is a good strategy?
practice_items.concept: Paraphrase it: the joint between the foot and the leg.

options: Paraphrase it: the joint between the foot and the leg.
Say the German word louder.

practice_items.question: In spoken mediation, how do you pass on what your dad says to the doctor?
practice_items.concept: In the third person: “My dad says that …”.
practice_items.sample_solution: You don't translate word for word in the first person. You report: “My dad says that he twisted his ankle yesterday.” Important numbers and instructions are passed on exactly.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Booking a room by phone“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Why is Review B more helpful than Review A?
practice_items.concept: It gives concrete positive and negative points with reasons.

options: It gives concrete positive and negative points with reasons.
It uses more exclamation marks.

practice_items.question: What makes an online review fair and helpful?
practice_items.concept: Concrete good and bad points with reasons and a recommendation.
practice_items.sample_solution: A helpful review says what you used and when, gives concrete positive and negative points with reasons, for example “clean room, but noisy at night”, and ends with a recommendation.

atoms.title: From New Amsterdam to New York

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Two settlements, two points of view“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: What was New York called when it was a Dutch settlement?
practice_items.concept: New Amsterdam

options: New Amsterdam
New England

practice_items.question: When was the Statue of Liberty dedicated, and who gave it?
practice_items.concept: In 1886; it was a gift from the people of France.
practice_items.sample_solution: The Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor was a gift from the people of France and was dedicated in 1886. It greeted many immigrants who arrived by ship.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „A radio ad and a store announcement“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which of these is one of New York City's five boroughs?
practice_items.concept: Brooklyn

options: Brooklyn
New Jersey

practice_items.question: How do you politely check an announcement you didn't hear clearly?
practice_items.concept: Repeat what you understood and ask: “Did they say …?”
practice_items.sample_solution: For example: “Excuse me, did they say the A train isn't stopping at 42nd Street?” The other person only has to confirm or correct the part you are unsure about.

practice_items.question: Which sentence correctly describes the picture?
practice_items.concept: In the foreground, a girl is waving a flag.

options: In the foreground, a girl is waving a flag.
In the background, a girl waves a flag every day.

practice_items.question: Which tense do you use to describe what is happening in a picture?
practice_items.concept: The present progressive, e.g. “A girl is waving a flag.”
practice_items.sample_solution: In picture descriptions the present progressive shows what is happening at the moment: “A family is eating at a table.” Places are given with in the foreground, in the middle and in the background.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „However, although, as a result“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which sentence compares the two cities correctly?
practice_items.concept: While LA is famous for films, Chicago is known for architecture.

options: While LA is famous for films, Chicago is known for architecture.
Chicago is more warmer than Los Angeles.

practice_items.question: Which word links two contrasting facts in one sentence: “___ LA is warm, Chicago has cold winters.”?
practice_items.concept: While (or whereas).
practice_items.sample_solution: “While LA is warm and dry, Chicago has cold, windy winters.” While and whereas link two facts that are different; both can start the first clause.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Fifty states and a capital district“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: How many provinces and territories does Canada have today?
practice_items.concept: Ten provinces and three territories.

options: Ten provinces and three territories.
Fifty states and one district.

practice_items.question: What are Canada's two official languages?
practice_items.concept: English and French.
practice_items.sample_solution: Canada has two official languages, English and French. Most people in Quebec speak French, while English is the main language in most other provinces.

atoms.title: A radio show about growing up bilingual

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Ten provinces, three territories“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Canadian English often uses British spellings. Which spelling would you expect in a Canadian school book?
practice_items.concept: colour

options: colour
color

practice_items.question: What does a Canadian speaker often mean with “eh?” at the end of a sentence?
practice_items.concept: A friendly “don't you agree?”, like German „oder?“.
practice_items.sample_solution: “It's cold today, eh?” invites the listener to agree. It is a typical feature of spoken Canadian English, similar to „oder?“ or „gell?“ in German.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Ten provinces, three territories“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.
Die Lektion knüpft an „Many nations, many ways of life“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which three groups of Indigenous peoples does Canada's Constitution recognise?
practice_items.concept: First Nations, Inuit and Métis

options: First Nations, Inuit and Métis
Inuit, Cherokee and Lakota

practice_items.question: Which Canadian territory has the capital Iqaluit?
practice_items.concept: Nunavut.
practice_items.sample_solution: Iqaluit is the capital of Nunavut, a territory in the far north of Canada where most people are Inuit and Inuktitut is an important language.

atoms.title: Canada and the US: close neighbours

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Ten provinces, three territories“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: What is special about the land border between Canada and the USA?
practice_items.concept: It is the longest international border in the world.

options: It is the longest international border in the world.
It is closed to tourists all year.

practice_items.question: Name two ways in which Canada and the USA work closely together.
practice_items.concept: Trade and defence, for example through NORAD.
practice_items.sample_solution: The two neighbours are linked by huge trade and investment flows that support millions of jobs, and they defend North America together through NORAD.

atoms.title: Mediating for a Canadian exchange student

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „At the doctor's: helping your dad“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: How do you best explain the German word “Brotzeit” to a Canadian guest?
practice_items.concept: It's a cold meal with bread, cheese or sausage.

options: It's a cold meal with bread, cheese or sausage.
It's “bread time”.

practice_items.question: A German word has no English equivalent while you mediate. What do you do?
practice_items.concept: Explain it with a paraphrase or an example.
practice_items.sample_solution: Instead of translating “Brotzeit” word for word, you explain: “It's a cold meal with bread, cheese and sausage.” A paraphrase or example tells the listener what is meant.

atoms.title: Myself – or no pronoun at all?

practice_items.question: How do you say „Wir haben uns am Bahnhof getroffen“ in English?
practice_items.concept: We met at the station.

options: We met at the station.
We met ourselves at the station.

practice_items.question: What are “sich treffen”, “sich erinnern” and “sich fühlen” in English?
practice_items.concept: meet, remember, feel – without a reflexive pronoun.
practice_items.sample_solution: “We met at the station.” “I remember the trip.” “I feel tired.” Many German „sich“-verbs are not reflexive in English, so no myself or ourselves follows.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Myself – or no pronoun at all?“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Mia helps Ben, and Ben helps Mia. Which sentence fits?
practice_items.concept: Mia and Ben help each other.

options: Mia and Ben help each other.
Mia and Ben help themselves.

practice_items.question: What does the pronoun show in “I made the poster myself”?
practice_items.concept: That I did it personally, without help.
practice_items.sample_solution: Here myself is an emphatic pronoun: it stresses the person. The sentence is still correct without it, but myself adds „selbst, ohne Hilfe“.

practice_items.question: Which sentence is correct?
practice_items.concept: Can you explain the rule to me?

options: Can you explain the rule to me?
Can you explain me the rule?

practice_items.question: How do you say „Erklär mir die Regel“ correctly in English?
practice_items.concept: Explain the rule to me.
practice_items.sample_solution: Explain, describe and suggest need to before the person: “Explain the rule to me.” With give, show or send both patterns work: “Show me the map” or “Show the map to me”.

atoms.title: Who called? – Who did you call?

practice_items.question: Your friend says, “Somebody called me.” Which question asks about that person?
practice_items.concept: Who called you?

options: Who called you?
Who did you call?

practice_items.question: When does a question with who or what need no do, does or did?
practice_items.concept: When who or what is the subject of the question.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Who called you?” asks for the subject (somebody called you), so there is no did. “Who did you call?” asks for the object (you called somebody), so it needs did.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Who called? – Who did you call?“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Your friend asks, “Don't you like pizza?” You DO like pizza. What do you answer?
practice_items.concept: Yes, I do.

options: Yes, I do.
No, I do.

practice_items.question: What does a negative question like “Isn't it beautiful?” often show?
practice_items.concept: That the speaker expects the answer yes or is surprised.
practice_items.sample_solution: Negative questions often show surprise (“Don't you know him?”) or that you expect agreement (“Isn't it beautiful?” – “Yes, it is.”). Why don't we …? makes a suggestion.

atoms.title: It was opened in 1883: the passive

practice_items.question: Which sentence is a correct passive in the simple past?
practice_items.concept: The bridge was opened in 1883.

options: The bridge was opened in 1883.
The bridge opened by the city in 1883.

practice_items.question: How do you form the passive in English?
practice_items.concept: A form of be + past participle.
practice_items.sample_solution: The tense is shown by be: “is used” (present), “was opened” (past), “will be repaired” (future), “can be bought” (modal). The past participle stays the same.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „It was opened in 1883: the passive“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.
Die Lektion knüpft an „Give someone something“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which passive sentence sounds the most natural in English?
practice_items.concept: I was offered a place in the choir.

options: I was offered a place in the choir.
To me was offered a place in the choir.

practice_items.question: Turn into the personal passive: “They offered her a job.”
practice_items.concept: She was offered a job.
practice_items.sample_solution: With verbs like give, offer, show, tell and promise, English often makes the person the subject: “She was offered a job.” German says „Ihr wurde ein Job angeboten“.

practice_items.question: You talk about a past situation that cannot be changed. Which type do you need?
practice_items.concept: Type 3: If I had known, I would have come.

options: Type 3: If I had known, I would have come.
Type 1: If I know, I will come.

practice_items.question: Which verb forms does a type 2 conditional use?
practice_items.concept: If + simple past, would + infinitive.
practice_items.sample_solution: “If I had a million dollars, I would travel around Canada.” Type 2 describes an unlikely or imagined situation; for advice people often say “If I were you, I would …”.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Type 0, 1, 2 – or 3?“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Complete the main clause of this type 3 conditional: “If you had asked me, I ___ (help) you.”
practice_items.concept: would have helped

options: would have helped
would help

practice_items.question: Which tense follows if in a type 3 conditional?
practice_items.concept: The past perfect (had + past participle).
practice_items.sample_solution: “If I had known, I would have come.” The if-clause uses the past perfect, the main clause would/could/might have + past participle. There is no would in the if-clause.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „It was opened in 1883: the passive“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: What does “Walking along the seawall, we saw a seal” mean?
practice_items.concept: While we were walking along the seawall, we saw a seal.

options: While we were walking along the seawall, we saw a seal.
The seal was walking along the seawall when we saw it.

practice_items.question: What kind of meaning does a past participle construction like “Built in 1883, the bridge …” have?
practice_items.concept: A passive meaning: the bridge, which was built in 1883, …
practice_items.sample_solution: Past participle constructions are passive: “Built in 1883, the bridge is still in use” means “The bridge, which was built in 1883, is still in use.” -ing constructions are active.

atoms.title: Will be able to, had to, allowed to

practice_items.question: Which sentence means that something is NOT necessary?
practice_items.concept: You don't have to bring a sleeping bag.

options: You don't have to bring a sleeping bag.
You mustn't bring a sleeping bag.

practice_items.question: What is the difference between “mustn't” and “don't have to”?
practice_items.concept: mustn't = not allowed; don't have to = not necessary.
practice_items.sample_solution: “You mustn't use your phone in the test” is a ban (darf nicht). “You don't have to bring a dictionary” means it is not necessary (muss nicht).

practice_items.question: You feel no interest during a long bus ride. What do you say?
practice_items.concept: I'm bored.

options: I'm bored.
I'm boring.

practice_items.question: What is the difference between “interesting” and “interested”?
practice_items.concept: interesting describes the thing; interested describes how a person feels.
practice_items.sample_solution: “The museum was interesting” describes the museum. “I was interested in the photos” describes my feeling. The same rule works for boring/bored and exciting/excited.

practice_items.question: Which sentence is correct?
practice_items.concept: I'm looking forward to meeting you.

options: I'm looking forward to meeting you.
I'm looking forward to meet you.

practice_items.question: Why do you say “I'm looking forward to meeting you” and not “to meet you”?
practice_items.concept: In look forward to, to is a preposition, so -ing follows.
practice_items.sample_solution: After a preposition English uses the -ing form. In look forward to, to is a preposition, not part of an infinitive: “I'm looking forward to meeting you.”

practice_items.question: Which sentence is correct?
practice_items.concept: We set it up in ten minutes.

options: We set it up in ten minutes.
We set up it in ten minutes.

practice_items.question: Where does a pronoun go with a separable phrasal verb like “set up”?
practice_items.concept: Between the verb and the particle: set it up.
practice_items.sample_solution: A noun can go before or after the particle (set up the tent / set the tent up), but a pronoun must go in the middle: “set it up”, not “set up it”.

practice_items.question: Which word is British English for the American word “apartment”?
practice_items.concept: flat

options: flat
sidewalk

practice_items.question: How do American and British English spell the word for „Farbe“?
practice_items.concept: AE color, BE colour.
practice_items.sample_solution: American English writes color, center and favorite; British English writes colour, centre and favourite. Both are correct, but one text should use one variety.

practice_items.question: “Unbelievable offer!” and “We'll offer you free delivery.” What has happened to the word “offer”?
practice_items.concept: Conversion: the same word is a noun and a verb.

options: Conversion: the same word is a noun and a verb.
Clipping: the word has been shortened.

practice_items.question: What is conversion in word building?
practice_items.concept: A word changes its word class without a new ending, e.g. to offer → an offer.
practice_items.sample_solution: In conversion the form stays the same, but the word class changes: to offer → an offer, a text → to text. The sentence (a/the, to, -s) shows you the word class.

practice_items.question: Which linking word shows a contrast?
practice_items.concept: however

options: however
in addition

practice_items.question: Name three linking words that introduce a contrast.
practice_items.concept: however, although, whereas (also: on the other hand).
practice_items.sample_solution: Contrast: however, although, whereas, on the other hand, nevertheless. Addition: in addition, furthermore. Result: as a result, therefore, that's why.

practice_items.question: Tom compares his little white streak with a “far-reaching continent of unwhitewashed fence”. What does this exaggeration show?
practice_items.concept: How hopeless the job feels to him.

options: How hopeless the job feels to him.
That the fence is really as big as a continent.

practice_items.question: Who wrote “The Adventures of Tom Sawyer” (1876)?
practice_items.concept: Mark Twain (Samuel L. Clemens).
practice_items.sample_solution: Mark Twain, whose real name was Samuel L. Clemens (1835–1910), grew up in Hannibal on the Mississippi and used memories of that childhood in “The Adventures of Tom Sawyer”.

atoms.title: Snow Day: continue or change a story

practice_items.question: Who tells the story “Snow Day”?
practice_items.concept: A third-person narrator who follows Maya.

options: A third-person narrator who follows Maya.
Maya herself, as an “I” narrator.

practice_items.question: What must a continuation of a story keep from the original?
practice_items.concept: The characters, the setting, the tense and the tone.
practice_items.sample_solution: When you continue a story, only the action goes on: the same characters, the same place, the same tense (usually the simple past) and the same tone, so that it fits the beginning.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Tom Sawyer and the fence“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which author wrote the anti-slavery novel “Uncle Tom's Cabin” (1852)?
practice_items.concept: Harriet Beecher Stowe

options: Harriet Beecher Stowe
Mark Twain

practice_items.question: What is James Thurber known for?
practice_items.concept: Humorous stories and drawings, e.g. “The Secret Life of Walter Mitty”.
practice_items.sample_solution: James Thurber (1894–1961) from Columbus, Ohio, wrote humorous stories and drew cartoons, many first published in The New Yorker; “The Secret Life of Walter Mitty” was filmed in 1947.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Tom Sawyer and the fence“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: You are reading a whole novel in English. Which strategy fits extensive reading?
practice_items.concept: Read on and guess unknown words from the context.

options: Read on and guess unknown words from the context.
Look up every unknown word at once.

practice_items.question: What do you write in a reading log after a reading session?
practice_items.concept: Pages, what happened, new words and your opinion.
practice_items.sample_solution: A reading log entry notes the pages, a short summary of the plot, a few new words and your opinion. It helps you to keep track of a whole book.

prerequisites.rationale: Die Lektion knüpft an „Explaining the Underground Railroad in German“ an; eigenständiger Einstieg bleibt möglich.

practice_items.question: Which phrase opens a presentation?
practice_items.concept: Today I'm going to talk about …

options: Today I'm going to talk about …
Are there any questions?

practice_items.question: What should you write on note cards for a presentation?
practice_items.concept: Key words, not full sentences.
practice_items.sample_solution: Note cards hold key words, names and numbers, so you can speak freely and look at your audience instead of reading full sentences aloud.

practice_items.question: You are researching how geysers work for a school project. Which result is the best place to start?
practice_items.concept: The National Park Service page, updated this year.

options: The National Park Service page, updated this year.
The sponsored ad for cheap hotels.

practice_items.question: Name three questions you ask to check a website as a source.
practice_items.concept: Who made it? When was it updated? Does it want to inform or to sell?
practice_items.sample_solution: Check who made the page (an authority, a museum, a company or an unknown person), when it was updated and what its purpose is. Ads are marked “Sponsored” or “Ad”.

practice_items.question: “Our class wants to record a podcast.” Where is the stress on “record”?
practice_items.concept: reCORD – on the second syllable, because it is a verb.

options: reCORD – on the second syllable, because it is a verb.
REcord – on the first syllable, because it is a noun.

practice_items.question: What does the mark ˈ show in a dictionary's pronunciation?
practice_items.concept: That the next syllable is stressed.
practice_items.sample_solution: In /rɪˈkɔːd/ the mark ˈ comes before the stressed syllable, so the verb record is stressed reCORD; the noun /ˈrekɔːd/ is stressed REcord.

practice_items.question: Your partner's text has good ideas but several tense mistakes. Which feedback is most helpful?
practice_items.concept: Your ideas are clear. Check the simple past forms in paragraph 2.

options: Your ideas are clear. Check the simple past forms in paragraph 2.
This is bad. Write it again.

practice_items.question: What do you write down in an error log (Fehlerprotokoll)?
practice_items.concept: The mistake, the correct form and a rule or example.
practice_items.sample_solution: For example: “I am boring.” → “I am bored.” (feelings: -ed). Writing down the rule helps you to avoid the same mistake next time.

practice_items.question: Which is the best research question for a mini-project?
practice_items.concept: Why is basketball so popular at American high schools?

options: Why is basketball so popular at American high schools?
Basketball.

practice_items.question: What makes a good research question for a project?
practice_items.concept: It is open, clear and can be answered with sources in the time you have.
practice_items.sample_solution: “Why is basketball so popular at American high schools?” is open (why/how), clear and answerable. “Basketball” is only a topic, and “Is basketball good?” is too vague.
